proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof, second half: 'by the monotonicity formula ... p_{S⊥}(x − y) = 0 for C-a.e. (x,S); thus (using the continuity of p_{S⊥}(x − y) in (x,S)) we have (8)'. Here G := Grassmannian N n.
Imports. Grassmannian.continuous_project lives in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.RadialFirstVariation, which GMT.Ch08.Submission does not import yet. Add `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.RadialFirstVariation`; its axioms are only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
1. Let w(z) := (z.1 − y) − project z.2 (z.1 − y) for z ∈ ℝ^N × G; this is p_{S⊥}(x − y) for z = (x,S). w is continuous. SimonGMT Grassmannian.continuous_project (RadialFirstVariation.lean) gives continuity of (S,v) ↦ project S v on G × ℝ^N; compose it with the continuous map z ↦ (z.2, z.1 − y), and subtraction is continuous.
2. The integrand g(z) := ofReal(|w(z)|²/|z.1 − y|^{n+2}) is measurable. The numerator and denominator are continuous real functions, their quotient is measurable (Measurable.div), and ofReal is measurable.
3. Fix ρ > 0. Then ∫_{B_ρ(y)×G} g dV = 0. By lintegral_eq_zero_iff, g = 0 a.e. for V restricted to B_ρ(y) × G. This product set is measurable, so by ae_restrict_iff', for V-a.e. z: z ∈ B_ρ(y) × G implies g(z) = 0.
4. Let z be such a point with z.1 ∈ B_ρ(y).
   - If z.1 ≠ y, then |z.1 − y|^{n+2} > 0. g(z) = 0 means |w(z)|²/|z.1 − y|^{n+2} ≤ 0, hence |w(z)|² ≤ 0, so w(z) = 0.
   - If z.1 = y, then w(z) = 0 − project z.2 0 = 0, because project z.2 is linear.
5. Apply steps 3–4 with ρ = k + 1 for every k ∈ ℕ and intersect the countably many full-measure sets (ae_all_iff). For V-a.e. z, for all k, z.1 ∈ B_{k+1}(y) implies w(z) = 0. Every z.1 lies in some B_{k+1}(y): choose k > |z.1 − y|. Hence w = 0 V-a.e.
6. F := {z : w(z) = 0} is closed, as the preimage of {0} under the continuous w, and its complement is V-null. The support of a measure is contained in every closed set of full measure (Measure.support_subset_of_isClosed), so w(z) = 0 for every z ∈ spt V.
7. For z ∈ spt V we get project z.2 (z.1 − y) = z.1 − y. So z.1 − y lies in the range of the projection map z.2.projectionLinearMap, which is z.2.plane by definition (Grassmannian.plane). ∎

normalDefect = 0 gives |w|²/|x−y|^{n+2} = 0 V-a.e. on each B_ρ(y)×G, hence w = 0 there (trivially also at x = y).
Radii k+1 exhaust ℝ^N, so w = 0 V-a.e.
{w = 0} is closed with null complement, so it contains spt V; project S v = v means v ∈ S.plane.
